andrew: Heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-selection tweak (prefer-fast-kernel for short seqs) we hit a spike in GPU OOMs on long-chat workloads. saw it on canary and prod. attaching quick blockmgr dump and a p99 trace.

maya: ugh. we expected a slight perf win for short requests, not fragmentation. do you have the block reuse stats?

andrew: paste below (trimmed):
```
block_mgr: total_blocks=4096 block_size=256kb used=2.8GB free=1.2GB fragmentation=38% compaction_runs=4
hot_blocks=600 cold_blocks=3500 reuse_rate=0.12 avg_reuse_latency=1.8ms
alloc_failures=23 last_oom=1847654308
```
The interesting bit: reuse_rate dropped after kernel change; compaction cost shot up.

simon: any correlation with batching? I remember a batching heuristic tweak last week (continuous-batch wait=8ms -> 4ms) that increased peak concurrent seqs. more simultaneous KV windows could increase working set.

andrew: yes — continuous batching was lowered on the same deploy. suspect two orthogonal changes combined. I've got one flamegraph from nvprof showing allocation hotspots during a long-generation (50+ tokens):
```
GPU timeline: 0-120ms: KV fetches
120-450ms: attention blocks allocate  (many small mallocs)
450-900ms: compaction + kernel fallback
kernel_select: fast_kernel chosen for many layers
```
compaction stalls coincide with kernel fallback times.

maya: hmm. idea: try hot/cold block segregation + per-model freelist buckets. hot blocks = ones accessed by KV cache in last N requests, cold = everything else. keep hot in front to increase reuse and avoid scanning. Also bound compaction to a budget per-request.

taylor: +1. We implemented a lightweight bucketed-freelist for the slab allocator in local experiments — reduced fragmentation by ~15% for encoder-heavy loads. Can spin up a branch with per-model pre-reserve workspace (reserve proportional to avg_seq_length * token_peak_factor).

andrew: nice. can you also add a safety cap on continuous-batch peak tokens? If we cap max_tokens_in_flight per-gpu we might avoid pathological peaks that force compaction.

perf-bot: Deploy 1847654200 reverted to 1847654000 due to mem OOM alerts (alert group: gpu-oom-prod).

simon: repro steps I used locally — grabs a long-chat trace and runs the blockmgr stress harness:
```
# run with increased concurrency
PYTEST_ADDOPTS="-k blockmgr_stress --concurrency=48 --model=resnet-chat-7b" ./scripts/run_perf.sh
```
Log snippet: 
```
E alloc_block: size=128kb attempt=3 free_scan_ms=42
E compaction: cost=186ms freed=24MB
E alloc_block: failed after compaction
```
This shows compaction often doesn't free usable contiguous space because of fragmentation pattern (many small cold fragments).

maya: experimental plan:
1) revert kernel-selection fast-path for layers > 2048 cache-size until we have allocator improvements.
2) enable hot/cold segregation (N=64 requests) + bucketed freelist sizes [32kb,64kb,128kb,256kb,512kb].
3) add per-gpu cap: max_tokens_in_flight=2e6 by default, with a per-customer override.
4) throttle continuous-batch if projected peak tokens exceed cap (soft drop / fallback to lower throughput kernel).

andrew: sounds good. can we also add metrics for "reuse_rate_by_bucket" and "compaction_cost_ms" per-model so we can A/B before/after?

taylor: will add those. Also propose an opportunistic compact routine that coalesces only when fragmentation>threshold and compaction_benefit_estimate > X (avoid worst-case compaction runs).

andrew: if we do hot/cold segregation, what's the cost of tracking last-access? extra atomic increments on KV hits could be noisy.

maya: cheap: maintain a 64-entry LRU ring per-blockmgr with probabilistic sampling on access (1/8). not full precision but prevents full scans.

simon: timeline? can we get a canary branch today? I can run stress harness overnight.

maya: I'll open a PR with the bucketed freelist + metrics + config flags. choose default off for fast rollout. aim for canary by EOD.

andrew: thanks. putting a hold on kernel-selection change until canary results. @perf-bot please watch for OOM alerts and auto-revert if rate > 5/hour. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: Watcher updated: gpu-oom-prod threshold set to 5/hour. Auto-revert enabled.

taylor: FYI I reproduced the compaction regression locally when kernel selected "fast_kernel" for intermediate layers: reuse rate fell ~5x. adding in per-layer kernel blacklist for long-seq models helps.

andrew: excellent debugging — let's keep the kernel blacklist as temporary guard and iterate on allocator improvements. I'll file a follow-up to track perf/regression tests.

maya: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4523 — includes bucketed freelist, hot/cold segmentation, metrics. defaults disabled.

simon: running canary now, will post results in the morning. good work team. :coffee:
